titleText.en: Saying 'what kind of an idiot doesn't know about the Yellowstone supervolcano' is so much more boring than telling someone about the Yellowstone supervolcano for the first time.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive's title attribute is preserved exactly as its truncated value, including the trailing space; the official English title attribute is complete. Vision read SI as I, ESTOY as STOY, OPORTUNIDAD as CPORTUNIDAD, split OSTRAS, missed Y in the product question, lost the accent in SÚPER, and severely misread the two lower-left infographic labels. The country names, product names, percentages, and Arabic-numeral quantities are audited exclusions; chart operators and punctuation are artwork or ordinary punctuation.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to make fun; to mock (with myself as the actor)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Burlarme combines burlar with attached me. In burlarse de, the attached pronoun marks the person doing the mocking, while de introduces the target.

example.es: Intento no burlarme de nadie.
example.en: I try not to make fun of anyone.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: of; required after burlarse before the target
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Burlarse uses de before the person or thing being mocked. Natural English normally expresses the whole pattern as ‘make fun of’ or ‘mock.’

example.es: No te burles de tu hermano.
example.en: Do not make fun of your brother.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Admite is the present form of admitir for one person or thing. A following que clause states what is acknowledged.

example.es: El autor admite que se equivocó.
example.en: The author admits that he was wrong.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: knows; is familiar with (a fact or subject)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Conocer often means being acquainted with a person, place, subject, or item of knowledge. It contrasts with saber used for knowing that a statement is true.

example.es: Ella conoce bien el tema.
example.en: She knows the subject well.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Sabe is the present form of saber for one person or thing. It expresses knowledge of information; before an infinitive it can instead mean ‘knows how to.’

example.es: Todo el mundo sabe la respuesta.
example.en: Everyone knows the answer.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to reach; to arrive at (a life stage)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Llegar keeps its ordinary arrival sense when a following a phrase names an age or stage, as in llegar a adulto or llegar a los treinta.

example.es: Al llegar a adulta, se mudó.
example.en: When she reached adulthood, she moved.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: De is fixed with media in the statistical expression de media. Its meaning comes from the complete expression rather than the usual possession or origin senses.

example.es: Llegan diez mensajes de media.
example.en: Ten messages arrive on average.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Media is the feminine noun for an average. In de media it describes a typical value across many cases.

example.es: La media es de ocho horas.
example.en: The average is eight hours.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Escuchando is the ongoing-action form of escuchar. It follows a form of estar to describe listening or hearing in progress.

example.es: Están escuchando la noticia.
example.en: They are hearing the news.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; part of enterarse
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Enterarse is a pronominal verb meaning to find out or learn some information. Se changes with the subject and stays beside the changed verb or attaches to an infinitive.

example.es: Se enteró ayer.
example.en: She found out yesterday.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Enteró is the completed-past form used with se for one person: se enteró. The information learned can follow de or be understood from context.

example.es: Carlos se enteró de la reunión.
example.en: Carlos found out about the meeting.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Nacer is the dictionary form for coming into life. Spanish commonly uses al nacer for ‘at birth’ or ‘when born.’

example.es: El bebé pesó tres kilos al nacer.
example.en: The baby weighed three kilos at birth.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tasa is a feminine noun for a rate, especially a quantity measured relative to a population or period.

example.es: La tasa de empleo aumentó.
example.en: The employment rate increased.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: birth rate; births in a population
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Natalidad refers to births considered as a demographic measure. Tasa de natalidad is the standard expression for a birth rate.

example.es: La natalidad bajó este año.
example.en: The birth rate fell this year.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Burlo is the present yo form used in me burlo de. Me marks the speaker as the actor in the pronominal expression, and de introduces the target.

example.es: No me burlo de sus preguntas.
example.en: I do not make fun of their questions.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Some speakers use les for a masculine or mixed plural group as the direct object. More widely taught standard usage would normally use los here; les is standard when the people are indirect recipients.

example.es: A esos alumnos les vi ayer.
example.en: I saw those students yesterday.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: they have (special form after a future cuando)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tengan is a special form of tener used after cuando when the event is still expected or hypothetical rather than presented as an established fact.

example.es: Llámame cuando tengan tiempo.
example.en: Call me when they have time.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Momentos is the plural of momento. It can refer to short stretches of time or particular occasions and situations.

example.es: Todos tenemos momentos difíciles.
example.en: We all have difficult moments.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: they tell; they recount (special form in a desired result)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cuenten is a special form of contar. It appears after para que when the telling is the desired or prevented result.

example.es: Habla bajo para que no cuenten el secreto.
example.en: Speak quietly so that they do not tell the secret.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pierdo is the present yo form of perder. With oportunidad it means missing or losing an opportunity.

example.es: Pierdo una oportunidad si no voy.
example.en: I miss an opportunity if I do not go.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to have it; in pasarlo bien, to have a good time
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pasarlo combines pasar with attached lo. In the fixed expression pasarlo bien, the two words describe enjoying oneself rather than physically passing an object.

example.es: Queremos pasarlo bien.
example.en: We want to have a good time.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: well; completes pasarlo bien, ‘have a good time’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Bien completes the fixed expression pasarlo bien. Its meaning belongs to the whole enjoyment expression rather than an evaluation of how a task was performed.

example.es: Lo pasamos bien en la fiesta.
example.en: We had a good time at the party.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ostras is a mild informal exclamation of surprise. Its literal noun meaning is ‘oysters,’ but no oysters are meant in this reaction.

example.es: ¡Ostras, qué sorpresa!
example.en: Wow, what a surprise!

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Súper is an informal shortened noun for supermercado. The written accent distinguishes its stressed pronunciation.

example.es: Voy al súper por leche.
example.en: I am going to the supermarket for milk.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Afortunados can be a masculine or mixed plural adjective or a noun for fortunate people.

example.es: Los afortunados recibieron entradas.
example.en: The lucky ones received tickets.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: for; begins por primera vez, ‘for the first time’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Por is fixed with primera vez in this time expression. Its meaning comes from the complete expression rather than a price, cause, path, or per-unit use.

example.es: Visitamos Granada por primera vez.
example.en: We visited Granada for the first time.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you express making fun of a person or thing?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching pronominal form of burlarse followed by de and the target.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The pronoun changes with the subject: me burlo, te burlas, se burla, and so on. De remains before what is mocked.

example.es: No debemos burlarnos de los demás.
example.en: We should not make fun of others.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you state that a number is an average?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use de media after the measured quantity or statement.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De media is a compact statistical expression meaning ‘on average.’

example.es: La clase dura cincuenta minutos de media.
example.en: The class lasts fifty minutes on average.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something happens for the first time?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Primera agrees with the understood feminine noun vez. The three words work together as a time expression.

example.es: Probó el mango por primera vez.
example.en: She tried mango for the first time.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you name the rate of births in a population?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The phrase is a demographic measure, often stated per year or per thousand inhabitants.

example.es: La tasa de natalidad varía por región.
example.en: The birth rate varies by region.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone has or wants to have a good time?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use the matching form of pasar with lo and bien; in an infinitive, use pasarlo bien.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The expression is fixed: lo normally stands before a changed form, as in lo pasamos bien, but attaches to the infinitive pasar.

example.es: Espero que lo paséis bien.
example.en: I hope you all have a good time.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does the comic treat an apparently obvious fact as a daily opportunity?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Because people continually reach the age at which they can encounter any familiar fact for the first time, so sharing it can be more enjoyable than mocking them for not already knowing it.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The comic estimates that roughly 1,300 people in Spain encounter a given piece of common knowledge for the first time each day. The product demonstration turns the calculation into a concrete moment of delighted discovery.
